newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money rates remain steady, demand rises.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money rates remain steady, demand rises.

text.p: Croatian money market rates remained steady amid good supply on Monday, dealers said.
"The demand for kuna funds had grown somewhat compared to last week, but there is still some 40 million kuna ($6.1 million) left on the supply side," dealer Jasenka Blagaic told Reuters.
She put fresh morning trade at 30.7 million kuna.
Banks had 100.7 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from Saturday's 10.9 million.
Call money loans made up most of the money market trade and were granted mainly at a steady 7.0 percent, though some sporadic deals were made at a previous 8.0-percent rate.
Some 30-day deals were agreed at 11 and 13 percent for commercial banks and at 15 percent for savings banks. A savings bank paid 19 percent for a smaller two-month loan.

Banks' accounts fell to 450 million on Saturday from 492 million the previous day. The weekend overnight trade totalled 22.4 million kuna, with seven banks seeking funds to cover their shortfalls. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075 ($ = 6.559 Croatian Kuna)
